title: Which sign goes in each box?
description: Six pairs of numbers are compared by their floors on the line. Floors above the ground are greater than floors below, and the floor lying higher is the greater number. One pair is checked by counting floors down.
teaching_notes: One idea: the floor that lies higher is the greater number. Watch for students who compare only the digits for floors below the ground.

video_script.why: The child compares each pair of numbers by seeing which floor lies higher in the tall block.
video_script.substitution: the book's own six pairs of numbers read as floors of the tall block
video_script.anchor: the floors of {{NAME_10}}, with six pairs of numbers to compare
video_script.payoff_line: Whichever floor lies higher is the greater number.

final_answer.spoken: less than, less than, less than, greater than, greater than and less than

names.{{NAME_10}}: the multi-storey block of floors above and below the ground, used as the model for integers

hold_back: Answer: a. <, b. <, c. <, d. >, e. >, f. <
never_show: a bigger digit read as a greater number below the ground
maths_rules: Compare by the height of the floor in the tall block.
−2 < +5; −5 < +4 (below the ground is lower than above it).
−5 < −3 (five floors down is lower than three floors down).
Check: −5 is five floors down, −3 is three floors down.
video_script.design: One idea: the higher floor is the greater number. One floor line throughout. Method as in the solved examples.

beats.on_screen: title card Less or Greater; the floor line of the tall block appears with six pairs of numbers, each with an empty box between them

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the floor line appears
marks.pairs: the six pairs are listed with an empty box in each
marks.ask: the question is written into the anchor band

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about the floors of {{NAME_10}}.
<bookmark mark='pairs'/>Six pairs of numbers are given, with an empty box in each pair.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which sign goes in each box, less than or greater than?

beats.on_screen: the six pairs stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board while the child thinks

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the floor line with the ground at 0, plus floors above in teal and minus floors below in amber; a down arrow is tagged lower

marks.line: the floors are drawn on one vertical line
marks.way: the solved example from the book is shown beside the line
marks.above: the teal floors are outlined above the amber floors

narration: <bookmark mark='line'/>Think of the floors on one line, from the top to the bottom.
<bookmark mark='way'/>We solve it the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='above'/>Floors above the ground lie higher than floors below it.

marks.given: the line Given is written with the six pairs
marks.rest: the last three pairs are written under the first three

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, six pairs of numbers.
Minus two and plus five, minus five and plus four, minus five and minus three.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Plus six and minus six, zero and minus four, zero and plus four.

beats.on_screen: To find: the sign, < or >, for each box

marks.find: the line To find is written under Given

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the sign for each box.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: −2 and −5 lie below the ground, +5 and +4 lie above: −2 < +5 and −5 < +4

marks.mixed: the first two pairs are circled
marks.low: the floors minus two and minus five are lit below the ground and the signs are filled

narration: <bookmark mark='mixed'/>Step one, the first two pairs have one floor below the ground and one above it.
<bookmark mark='low'/>The floor below the ground lies lower.
Minus two is less than plus five.
Minus five is less than plus four.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: −5 is 5 floors down and −3 is 3 floors down, so −5 < −3

marks.far: floor minus five is outlined below floor minus three and the sign is filled

narration: <bookmark mark='both'/>Step two, minus five and minus three are both below the ground.
Minus five is five floors down, and minus three is three floors down.
<bookmark mark='far'/>Minus five lies further down, so it is less than minus three.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: +6 lies above the ground and −6 lies below it, so +6 > −6

marks.six: floor plus six is lit above the ground and floor minus six below it, and the sign is filled

narration: <bookmark mark='six'/>Step three, plus six lies above the ground, and minus six lies below it.
Plus six is greater than minus six.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: 0 is the ground floor, so 0 > −4 and 0 < +4

marks.four: floor plus four is lit above the ground floor and the last sign is filled

narration: <bookmark mark='zero'/>Step four, zero is the ground floor.
Minus four lies below it, so zero is greater than minus four.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Plus four lies above it, so zero is less than plus four.

beats.on_screen: Step 5: check the third pair, count floors down from 0: 5 floors down is lower than 3 floors down

marks.check: the lift counts down from the ground floor
marks.ok: floors minus three and minus five are lit and the sign is ticked

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, check the third pair by counting floors down from zero.
<bookmark mark='ok'/>Five floors down is lower than three floors down, which agrees with less than.

beats.on_screen: Answer: a. <, b. <, c. <, d. >, e. >, f. <

marks.ans: the answer line is boxed on the working board
marks.pay: the higher floor of each pair is outlined

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The signs are less than, less than, less than, greater than, greater than and less than.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>Whichever floor lies higher is the greater number.
